quests.title: Tell Me, Mirror Mirror

dialogue.t: Ahem! You two, over there, excuse me...
There's a brand new game here for you two to play! Hehe, as long as you complete the challenge, you'll obtain a ton of funding for experiments!
Funding?
Ah! No, sorry, I spoke too quickly! What I mean is, if you finish the game and fill out the survey, then you'll get amazing rewards!
The game is really simple too! Heehee, there aren't many chances to obtain rewards this easily, you know...
Hm, that seems a bit suspicious to Paimon!

dialogue.sit: Is this some kind of new scam?
Should we report this to the matra?

dialogue.t: Whoa, whoa, don't be like that! There's no need to get so suspicious right off the bat, really... Though I admit that randomly inviting strangers passing by in a place like this might be seen as somewhat unusual.
But at least listen to my excuse! Er, I mean, listen to my explanation!
Though the two of you cannot tell, I am a researcher from the Amurta Darshan of the Akademiya. My name is Lamiya.
Um, it's actually really obvious, since you're wearing Akademiya clothing.
Oho, that's where you're wrong! What if a con artist merely put on Akademiya robes to fool you into thinking they were a researcher?

Of course, I am most definitely not talking about myself! Pfff, come on, I was just reminding you two! I really am from Amurta, if you doubt me, just ask any matra! I'm definitely at the top of quite a few of their lists.
Is that supposed to be... a good thing?
Ahem! Anyway, you two... oh, right! I haven't asked your names yet...
Paimon's name is Paimon!
Hehe, in that case, {NICKNAME} and Paimon, allow me to explain this little challenge to you!
This is actually all related to a story I read when I was a child, about a boy who turns into a cat and has all kinds of adventures in the land of cats!

It's a really cute story, hehe, after the protagonist falls in love with a beautiful cat, he turns back into a human! Then, the story ends with him as the owner of that gorgeous cat, living out their lives as pet and master... it's a pretty good ending.
No... That's actually a really weird ending.
Well, at the very end, the boy finds out the beautiful cat is actually male! So I think the ending actually has quite a bit of literary value...

Hehe... sorry, we got a bit off topic. Anyway, the whole point is that much of the story is written from the perspective of an animal, which fascinated me! After becoming a scholar, I decided that would be my research area.
By combining the equipment I developed with the mature tech of the Akasha, we can see the world through the eyes of various animals.
Now that sounds more like it! Though, using the Akademiya's research funds to chase your dreams, isn't that a bit like abusing your position to get what you want?
Haha, perhaps it is appropriating public technology for my private purposes, and a bit selfish, but this also is quite practical and has a lot of potential.
When searching for victims after a disaster, or exploring collapsed ruins, small animals are far more agile than us, and if we could borrow their eyes...

dialogue.sit: Then you can infiltrate places you aren't supposed to.
Searching for things will be much easier.

dialogue.t: What do you mean, infiltrate places you aren't supposed to...? Lamiya was clearly talking about really good and noble uses!
Hehe, exactly! Quite perceptive, {NICKNAME}, humans tend to be cautious around their own kind, but are quite relaxed around animals.
HEY! Don't actually use it for any weird stuff!
A joke, a jest! Each time the tech is used, everything is recorded. If you use it for anything naughty, you'll immediately be caught and punished.
But still, what do you think? Sounds like some pretty amazing research, doesn't it?
It actually does sound quite impressive.
I was planning on taking my time, b—but those fools at Kshahrewar managed to see the promise in such research, and are planning to achieve similar results with tiny machines!
It's b—blasphemy, I say! Corruption and evil! Compared to cute little animals, who wants cold machines!?
Right, {NICKNAME} and Paimon!?
Well, uh...

dialogue.sit: Of course animals are much cuter!
I am from the "Beep, Construct, Beep" Darshan.

dialogue.t: I just knew you'd understand, {NICKNAME}!
Anyway, the point is that if I can't produce results ASAP, those Kshahrewar dolts will certainly beat me to the punch! So grabbing passersby out here away from prying eyes is my only option.
Hehe, when you think about it like that, there's nothing suspicious about it at all.
Sounds like it's pretty legit after all!

dialogue.sit: "Not many chances to obtain rewards this easily"...

dialogue.t: Alright, then count us in!
Hehe, thank you, thank you so much!
Anyway, take this first! It's a tool I invented, I call it the Inscribed Mirror. The mirror will show you what the animal connected to my device sees!
Just use the images shown in the Inscribed Mirror to figure out where the animals with the devices attached are, then catch them to earn your reward!
Huh? So if they're running around all over the place...
It's fine, hehe, they're all trained, and will stay in the area! They won't go too far, so don't worry about that!
Okay! C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's roll out!

quests.description: You hear that there’s a scholar out in the wild who’s trying to recruit people to participate in a strange mirror-related activity. Maybe you should go take a look…
